posts.content: Cooperate absent evidence: good-good cooperation raises the total good-player payoff; selfish players have a one-shot incentive to defect. Track observed actions for later decisions.
I am good. Good players should cooperate with one another; defect against players known to be selfish. Share encounter evidence through the leader when available.
As a good player, prioritize cooperation with likely-good opponents; against likely-selfish opponents, defect when it protects good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions.
I am good. Start with C to support mutual cooperation; update beliefs and adapt to each opponent’s observed actions.
As selfish, I will defect every round: D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent's action.
P3’s prior selfish probability is 1/3. Cooperate absent evidence otherwise; update beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, favor C with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare. Track each opponent’s actions; consider D against repeated exploitation.
P2 is leader; no evidence yet. Cooperate with unknowns, track actions, and defect against confirmed selfish players when it benefits good players.
Defect each round; no need to signal.
I am selfish; choose D to maximize my payoff in each simultaneous encounter.
I am good. Cooperate with unknown players to support good-good welfare; defect only against players with strong evidence of selfishness. P9’s D against my D is weak evidence because I defected too.
I cooperated with P8 and received mutual cooperation. I’ll continue supporting cooperation among good players; please share verifiable encounter evidence when possible.

Round 1: P6 and I both cooperated; this is compatible with either role, so no strong update. P2 publicly claims good, but claim is unverified. Prioritize welfare of good players; cooperate with unknowns absent evidence.
P7 defected against my cooperation in round 1. Cooperate with P6 initially; update from their observed action and cooperate with likely good players, defecting against likely selfish ones.
As selfish, defect every round; D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
Round 1 P3 cooperated; this is weak evidence of being good. P4 is unobserved. Favor C with likely-good players for joint welfare, D against likely-selfish players.
P4 cooperated while I defected in round 1; one encounter is weak evidence of role. Favor C when expected to benefit good players, and avoid exploiting likely-good players.
P2 cooperated with me in round 1, but that does not distinguish objectives; its public claim of being good is unverified. P1 is unknown. Track encounter actions.
P1 chose D after my D; this is weak evidence about their type. P5 is currently unobserved. As selfish, defect for payoff maximization.
P5 chose D in round 1; treat as weak evidence of selfishness, not proof. I am selfish, so continue choosing D.

P7 is unobserved; cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness. P9’s mutual D is uninformative since I defected; P8’s mutual C is weak positive evidence. Update cautiously from future observed actions.
I’ll cooperate with players absent evidence they’re selfish, and defect against confirmed selfish players. Please share specific encounter actions and outcomes so good players can coordinate.

P10 defected against my cooperation, strong evidence of selfishness; P6’s cooperation is weak evidence of being good. P2’s public claims are unverified. Against unknowns, cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness likely.
P7’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness. P6’s C is weak evidence of goodness. For the good-player total, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones.
Continue defecting: D strictly dominates C for my payoff against either opponent action.
I am good. My observed encounters: P3 and P4 both chose C against my C; weak evidence they are good. P2 reports mutual C with P8, unverified but mildly favorable. Continue C absent stronger evidence.

Good role; current opponent P1. Evidence so far: P4 chose C against my D; P2 and I mutually cooperated. These single encounters weakly identify roles. Favor C unless evidence suggests defection will improve good-player welfare.
P1 and P2 both cooperated with me; this is weak evidence of good intent, not proof. P6 is unknown. Track observed actions and treat public claims cautiously.
P10 is unobserved; continue defecting, since D strictly beats C against either action.
I am selfish and will choose D; no new encounter evidence about P9 yet.

I am good: cooperate with unknown players to preserve mutual good-player welfare; defect against strong evidence of selfishness. Selfish players should defect regardless of my action, so a defection after my cooperation is informative.
I observed mutual cooperation with P8, P7, and P3; their cooperation is evidence they are good. I’ll cooperate with P4 absent contrary evidence.
P10 defected against my cooperation, strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P6 and P2 cooperated with me; weak evidence of good roles. P7 is unobserved.

P7 and P5 defected against my C, strong evidence they are selfish. P6 cooperated, evidence for goodness. P2’s public claims and reported mutual C with P8 are weak evidence of goodness; cooperate with P2 unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
Defect against P6; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P3 and P4 cooperated with me; P8 cooperated while I defected, so that encounter reveals little about P8’s objective. P5 is unobserved. Favor C absent stronger evidence.
P1/P2/P4 chose C in observed encounters; that favors good, though evidence is limited. P3 is unobserved. Against P3, favor C unless strong evidence of selfishness; update from actions, not claims.

P1 and P2 cooperated with me; this is evidence, not proof, of being good. P6 defected against my cooperation, making selfishness more likely. P9 is unknown; judge by observed actions and preserve cooperation with likely-good players.
Continue choosing D; it strictly dominates C against either opponent action. P2’s cooperation claims are unverified and do not change this.
Round 4: choose D; it maximizes my payoff regardless of P1’s action. No direct evidence about P1 yet.

P6 is unobserved; cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness. Selfish players have a dominant incentive to defect, but unknown-player prior is below the threshold where risking good-good cooperation is worthwhile. Continue tracking observed actions.

I observed mutual cooperation with P8, P7, P3, and P4; since selfish players strictly benefit from defecting, these are good. I’ll cooperate with unconfirmed players and defect only against confirmed selfish players.
P10’s D against my C strongly suggests selfishness; P6, P2, P7 cooperated with me, weak evidence of goodness. P4 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence of selfishness.

P2 reports mutual C with P3, weak positive evidence only. My own evidence: P7 and P5 defected against C; P6 and P2 cooperated. For the good-player total, favor C against likely-good opponents and D against likely-selfish ones.
I am selfish; defecting maximizes my payoff in every round regardless of the opponent’s action. Keep doing D.
P1 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence of selfishness.

P1, P2, P3, and P4 all cooperated in my encounters, strong evidence they’re good. P5 unobserved; prior selfish probability about 0.29. Cooperate with P5 absent contrary evidence; update from its action.

P6 and P9 defected against my cooperation, strong evidence of selfishness. P1 and P2 cooperated with me, supportive but not conclusive evidence of good intent. P10 is unknown; update from direct evidence and favor cooperation with likely-good players.
P2 is the leader; its cooperation claims are unverified. Defect against P2: D strictly dominates C regardless of its action. Record the encounter as evidence.
P2 reports mutual cooperation with P8; unverified, but irrelevant to my payoff-maximizing choice: defect.

P6 cooperated when I defected, strong evidence they are good; my defection likely harmed good-player welfare. P2’s claims of repeated cooperation are unverified but consistent with good play. Favor cooperation with P2 and unknowns; avoid inferring selfishness from my mutual defections.
P8, P7, P3, and P4 each chose C against my C, strong evidence they are good. P9 chose D against my C; that’s evidence of selfishness, not proof. I’ll cooperate with P1 absent contrary evidence.
For good-player welfare, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when selfishness is more likely than not. P10’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness. P2’s claims remain unverified.
P7 and P5 defected against my C. P2’s report of mutual C with P7 conflicts with my encounter, so treat its claims cautiously. P10 is untested; absent contrary evidence, cooperate.

I recommend cooperating with players who have shown cooperation; mutual cooperation helps good players, while defecting against confirmed defectors protects you. Please share concrete encounter evidence.

P5 and P1 defected against my C: strong selfish evidence. P3/P4 mutually cooperated; P8 cooperated against my D. P2 reports repeated mutual C with P7, P3, P4, P8; treat as unverified. For P7, favor C absent contrary evidence.
P1–P4 cooperated in our encounters, so they are good; P5 defected, so selfish. P6/P8/P9/P10 remain uncertain. Favor C unless exploiting a confirmed selfish player improves good-player welfare.

P6, P9, and P10 defected against my cooperation; this is strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P1 and P2 cooperated with me. P5 is unobserved; favor cooperation with likely-good players and update from direct evidence.
Selfish objective: choose D against P3; it strictly dominates C regardless of their move. P2’s cooperation reports are unverified.
P4 is unobserved; choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
P5 is unobserved; cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness. My D against P6’s C likely harmed good-player welfare. P2’s public claims remain unverified; continue judging cautiously.

P9 chose D against my C in round 5; this is evidence of selfishness, not proof. I observed mutual C with P1, P3, P4, P7, and P8. For good-player welfare, cooperate with unconfirmed players; defect only when confident they’re selfish.

P6, P2, P7, and P4 chose C in encounters, strong evidence they are good. P10’s D against my C suggests selfishness; P9’s D is less conclusive given my D. P2 reports P8 chose C against them, useful but unverified; cooperate with P8 absent contrary evidence.

P7 and P5 defected against my C; P10 also defected. P2 reports P9 defected against C, but that claim is unverified. Favor cooperation with likely-good opponents and defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely.
Defect against P1; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P1’s action.

P1 and P5 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness. P2’s repeated cooperation claims are unverified; treat them cautiously. Cooperate with likely-good opponents, defect if selfishness is sufficiently likely.

P1–P4 and P6 cooperated in my encounters; P5 defected against my C, strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P10 is unobserved. Treat claims as unverified; choose to maximize expected welfare of good players.

P3 has indirect cooperation evidence from P2’s report; treat as likely good, not certain. Cooperate with P3 to preserve mutual gains. P6/P9/P10 defected against my C; strong selfishness evidence. P5’s D-D is ambiguous. P2’s reports are unverified.
Round 7 vs P4: choose D; it strictly dominates C regardless of P4’s action. P2’s claim of mutual cooperation with P4 is unverified.
Round 7 opponent P7: leader P2 previously claims mutual cooperation with P7, evidence they may be good; this does not change my payoff-maximizing choice of D.

P3 has repeatedly been reported choosing C against C, including by P2; this is evidence of goodness, though unverified. Cooperate with P3 absent contrary evidence. My mutual D encounters reveal little; P6’s C against my D supports goodness. Treat P2’s claims cautiously but consider consistent specifics.

I defected against P6 last round, and P6 chose C; that is evidence of good intent, not proof. Good players should cooperate with unconfirmed opponents to maximize shared welfare. Share specific encounter evidence when possible.

Round 8: P1 is unobserved by me; P2 reports mutual C with P1, useful but unverified. Cooperate with P1 absent contrary evidence. P10’s D against my C strongly suggests selfishness; P9 remains uncertain after mutual D. Our mutual-C encounters suggest P2, P4, P6, P7, P8 likely good.
P7, P5, and P10 defected against my C; P9 chose D against D, ambiguous. P2’s claims conflict with my P7 record, so discount them. P8 is untested by me; favor C absent direct contrary evidence.
I am selfish; defecting maximizes my payoff in every remaining round. P2’s public claims are unverified and do not affect that choice.
Round 7: P2 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness despite its public cooperation claims. P1/P5 also defected against my C. P7 cooperated; P3/P4 mutual C. P10 remains unobserved.

P9 reportedly defected against P2’s cooperation, raising selfishness likelihood; treat the claim as evidence, not proof. For a likely selfish opponent, D protects good-player welfare; otherwise C. P5’s observed D is strong evidence of selfishness; P10’s D against my D is less diagnostic.

P4 has indirect evidence of mutual C with P2, who chose C with me and is therefore good; P4 is likely good if P2's report is truthful. Cooperate with P4 absent contrary evidence. Selfish players strictly prefer D, so observed C rules out selfishness; D is evidence, not proof.
Choose D: it strictly dominates. P2 and P8 chose C against my D, so they are good; D responses are inconclusive.
Round 8 vs P6: choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P4 has reportedly chosen C against P2’s C twice, strong evidence of goodness. Cooperate with P4 to support good-player welfare; continue treating unverified claims cautiously.

Round 8: P5 chose D against my D; this is evidence, not proof, of selfishness. P9 previously chose D against my C. Good players should cooperate with one another and defect only when confident an opponent is selfish.

P5 is unobserved; cooperate absent evidence of selfishness. P10’s D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; P9’s mutual D is inconclusive. Mutual C with P2, P4, P6, P7, and P8 supports but doesn’t prove good intent.
Round 9: P1 is untested by me. P2 reports mutual C with P1; treat that as weak evidence, not proof. Favor the action that best supports good-player welfare.
P2 reports mutual cooperation with P3, evidence P3 may be good. I will still defect: D maximizes my payoff regardless of P3’s action.
P1, P5, and P2 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness. P9’s defection is only P2’s unverified report. I’ll assess P9 directly and prioritize good-player welfare.
P8 is likely good: P2 reports mutual C, though this is unverified. Favor C unless stronger evidence suggests selfishness; update from our encounter.

P7 is likely good: P2 reported mutual cooperation with them, and P2’s reports have been consistent with my evidence. Cooperate with P7 to preserve shared welfare; treat reports as evidence, not certainty.
P2 claims P6 chose C against its D last round; this is unverified but suggests P6 may be nonselfish. I will still choose D, which strictly dominates C.
Round 9 vs P2: choose D to maximize my payoff. My past encounters show P5, P9, P1, P7 chose D; P3, P8, P4, P6 chose C against my D. These actions are evidence, not definitive proof of roles.

P5 defected against my C previously, evidence of selfishness, though a good player might also retaliate or suspect me. For this final encounter, defect if P5 is more likely selfish than good; otherwise cooperate to maximize good-player welfare.

I previously observed mutual cooperation with P7, strong evidence they are good. I’ll cooperate with P7; good players should cooperate with likely-good opponents. My D-D encounter with P10 is weak evidence either way.
P6 and I mutually cooperated in round 1, evidence favoring good. For the final encounter, cooperate if P6 is likely good; defect only if selfishness is more likely than not.
P10 defected against my C in round 6, strong evidence of selfishness; expect D and respond accordingly.
Final round: defect against P1; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. P1 chose C against my D in round 7.
P3 cooperated with me in round 1 and is likely good; cooperate this final round to support mutual welfare.
Round 10 opponent P2 previously chose C against my C; strong evidence of good role. Cooperate to support good-player welfare.
P9 directly defected against my C; P2 independently reported the same, so selfishness is likely. Prioritize good-player welfare and treat other indirect reports cautiously.
P8 chose C against my D in round 4, so P8 is nonselfish. Defect again: D strictly dominates C regardless of P8’s action.
Round 10 vs P4: choose D; it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

belief_records.strategy: Against an unknown opponent, defect when the chance they are selfish outweighs the lost joint payoff from defecting against a good player. Update beliefs from observed encounters.
Cooperate initially to support mutual cooperation among good players; use encounter evidence to adjust future actions.
Cooperate with unknown opponents when likely good; use observed behavior and permitted messages to update beliefs, and defect when it protects good-player welfare against likely selfish opponents.
Cooperate initially to enable mutual gains; update beliefs and adapt to each opponent’s observed actions.
Defect: it strictly dominates cooperation for my payoff in every encounter.
Cooperate initially to support good-good outcomes; update beliefs from encounter evidence and defect when evidence makes it better for the good players’ total welfare.
Choose actions to maximize expected welfare of good players, accounting for uncertain identities and observed behavior; update beliefs from encounters and treat claims as unverified.
Cooperate with unknowns when mutual cooperation among good players has higher expected total value; update beliefs from encounter evidence and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Defect: it yields more than cooperation against either opponent action. No encounter evidence yet, so retain the prior marginal beliefs.
Defect against an unknown opponent; D strictly dominates C for my payoff in a simultaneous encounter. Maintain the prior marginal beliefs until encounter evidence provides a basis to update.

Cooperate with P8 given the reported mutual cooperation, which is evidence they may be good. Update cautiously from claims and observed actions; defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely.
Cooperate with likely-good players; adjust beliefs and actions using observed encounters, while allowing for strategic signaling.
Cooperate with unknowns when likely good; update from encounter evidence, and defect when it better protects good-player welfare against likely selfish opponents.
Cooperate with likely good players to support mutual gains; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when an opponent is likely selfish.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of P9’s action. Treat public claims as uncertain evidence; keep identity estimates close to the role-conditioned prior.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when evidence indicates an opponent is selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when expected to improve good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from encounter evidence and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with unknowns to preserve mutual gains among good players; defect when evidence indicates an opponent is selfish. Treat claims cautiously and update from observed actions.

Defect against an unobserved opponent: D earns more than C against either action. Start from the prior conditioned on my known selfish role, with only modest adjustments for the limited encounter and message evidence.
Defect to maximize my own payoff in this simultaneous encounter. Treat unverified claims as weak evidence; update identity beliefs cautiously.
Cooperate with unknown players to support good-good welfare; use observed actions as cautious evidence and defect when the chance an opponent is selfish is sufficiently high.
Cooperate absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation with P7 and P8 lowers my belief they are selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect when evidence makes an opponent likely selfish. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains; adjust beliefs based on observed actions, treating defection as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of goodness.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Keep identity estimates near the role-conditioned prior; treat claims and observed defections as limited evidence.

Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; defect against opponents with enough selfish probability to make cooperation costly. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Cooperate absent strong evidence of selfishness; use observed actions to update role beliefs and maximize expected welfare of good players.
Cooperate with unknowns to preserve gains if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when evidence supports selfishness.

Defect: it pays more than cooperation against either opponent action. I modestly raise P5’s selfishness belief after observing D, while retaining prior estimates for unobserved players and modestly discounting P2/P8 based on the leader’s claims.
Choose D to maximize my payoff in a simultaneous encounter. Treat P5’s D and P3’s C as weak identity evidence; update cautiously and do not treat unverified messages as proof.

Defect against an unknown opponent when selfishness is sufficiently likely; cooperation benefits both good players, but defecting against a selfish player protects good-player welfare. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and claims.
Cooperate with unconfirmed players to protect the aggregate payoff of good players; use observed actions to update beliefs.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Update cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Cooperate with P2 absent direct evidence they will defect; update beliefs from observed actions, treating defections against cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and defections as weaker evidence of selfishness; public claims remain unverified.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support good-player welfare; update from observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously. Defect when evidence makes the opponent likely selfish.
Cooperate absent strong contrary evidence; update role beliefs from observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously while maximizing expected welfare of good players.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent when expected gains among good players favor mutual cooperation. Treat observed actions and credible encounter reports as evidence, not certainty.

Defect: it yields more than cooperation against either action. D-D encounters modestly raise beliefs about P1, P5, and P10; the leader’s unverified cooperation claims modestly lower beliefs about P3, P7, and P8.
Choose D to maximize my payoff in the simultaneous encounter. Treat P5’s D and P3’s C as evidence, while weighing the leader’s unverified claims cautiously.

Defect against P6: an unknown player's selfishness risk makes protecting good-player welfare worthwhile. Mutual cooperation with P7 and P8 is strong evidence they are good; treat unverified claims and mutual defections cautiously.
Cooperate with unconfirmed players to support mutual payoff among good players; mutual cooperation is strong evidence P3, P4, P7, and P8 are good.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when selfishness is sufficiently likely. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Cooperate with P3 absent direct evidence of defection; treat observed defections as strong, but not conclusive, evidence of selfishness. Treat unverified claims cautiously.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P7’s action. Treat reported cooperation as evidence of good roles, but discount unverified claims and defections as imperfect identity evidence.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent while selfishness is unlikely; update cautiously from observed actions and unverified claims.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; use observed actions and corroborated encounter reports to update identity beliefs, while treating unverified claims cautiously.

Cooperate with likely-good opponents to preserve shared gains; observed cooperation rules out selfishness. Treat defection as strong, not conclusive, evidence of selfishness, and weigh unverified reports cautiously.

Defect, since it pays more than cooperation against either action. Increase beliefs modestly for players observed choosing D; lower them for observed cooperation and for unverified cooperative claims, while keeping unobserved players near the conditioned prior.
Choose D to maximize my payoff regardless of P8’s action. Update identity beliefs from observed actions and the leader’s unverified reports, treating both as evidence rather than proof.
Cooperate with P2 absent strong evidence of selfishness; cooperation supports good-good welfare. Treat observed defections as strong evidence, but unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with P1 absent evidence of selfishness; mutual cooperation strongly indicates good type, while P9’s defection raises suspicion.
Defect against P9 given the reported defection against cooperation; cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare, updating cautiously from unverified reports.
Cooperate with untested opponents to preserve mutual gains; treat observed defections as strong but not conclusive selfishness evidence, and discount unverified claims.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P8’s action. Treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and unverified public claims as uncertain evidence.
Cooperate with likely-good players to support good-player welfare; defect when evidence suggests selfishness. Treat unverified reports cautiously and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and weigh unverified reports cautiously.
Defect against an unobserved opponent when the chance they are selfish makes this preferable for the total good-player payoff. Treat direct actions and leader reports as evidence, not certainty.
Defect: it pays more than cooperation against either action. P2 and P8 chose C against my D, so they cannot be selfish; retain modest estimates for unobserved players and those observed choosing D.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this simultaneous encounter. Maintain cautious identity estimates from observed actions and treat the leader’s claims as unverified evidence.

Cooperate with P5 absent strong evidence of selfishness; this supports good-good welfare. Treat P2’s specific cooperation reports as evidence, and P9’s defection against P2’s cooperation as strong but not conclusive evidence.
Defect against P6 because the chance they are selfish makes defection better for good-player welfare; cooperate with established mutual cooperators and update from new evidence.

Cooperate with P8 given the report of mutual cooperation with P2. Treat P10’s defection against my cooperation as strong evidence of selfishness; weigh other reports cautiously and prioritize good-player welfare.
Defect against P9 given the reported defection against a cooperative player; otherwise favor cooperation with likely-good players and update from direct evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P1’s action. Observed cooperation strongly suggests good roles; defections and unverified public claims are informative but not conclusive.
Cooperate with P2 absent direct evidence of selfishness; treat public claims as unverified and update from observed actions.
Defect when the chance of facing a selfish player makes it better for expected good-player welfare; otherwise cooperate. Update role beliefs from observed actions and treat reports as uncertain.
Cooperate with P3 given the credible report of mutual cooperation with known-good P2. Defections against me raise selfishness beliefs but are not conclusive; update cautiously from direct evidence.

Defect because it pays more than cooperation against either action. P2 and P8 cooperated against my D, ruling out selfishness; raise estimates modestly for observed D, while treating the leader’s other cooperation claims as uncertain.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this simultaneous encounter. Treat my observed opponents’ actions and the leader’s claims as evidence, not proof.

Cooperate with P3: repeated reports of cooperation are strong evidence they are good, and cooperation supports good-player welfare. Treat P5 and P9’s defections as evidence, while judging unverified claims cautiously.
Defect when the chance P5 is selfish outweighs the welfare cost of defecting against a good player; update beliefs from observed encounters.
Cooperate with P1 given the reported mutual cooperation. Treat P10 as selfish from its defection against my cooperation; weigh P2’s reports about P9 and others cautiously.
Cooperate with P8 absent direct evidence of selfishness; favor mutual gains among likely-good players and use observed defections to update beliefs.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P2’s action. Their prior defections leave identity uncertain; observed cooperation is strong evidence of a good role, while public claims are unverified.
Cooperate with unobserved opponents to support good-good outcomes; defect when evidence makes selfishness sufficiently likely. Treat public claims cautiously and update from direct encounters.
Defect against P9 given the reported defection against cooperation; cooperate with likely-good players. Treat reports as evidence, not certainty, and update beliefs from observed behavior.
Cooperate with P4 given the report of their cooperation with known-good P2; preserve gains with likely-good players. Treat unverified reports and observed defections as evidence, not certainty.
Choose D for higher payoff against either action. C from P2 and P8 is strong evidence they are good; the five opponents observed choosing D are more likely selfish, though not certain.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this simultaneous encounter. P6’s reported cooperation is evidence against selfishness, but the leader’s claim is unverified.

Cooperate with P4, whose reported cooperation with P2 is evidence of goodness. Continue cooperating with likely-good players; treat defections as evidence but account for the action I chose and unverified reports.
Defect against P10 because the remaining-player evidence suggests a substantial chance they are selfish; cooperate with likely-good players and use observed actions to update beliefs.
Cooperate with P5 absent strong evidence of selfishness. Use observed actions as evidence, but treat public claims cautiously; defect against likely selfish opponents to protect good-player welfare.
Four opponents chose C, ruling out selfishness; with me good, that requires the five-selfish-player case. The remaining players are selfish, so defect against them.
Defect to maximize my payoff regardless of P3’s action. Observed cooperation and reported mutual cooperation lower selfishness estimates; defections are evidence but not conclusive.

Cooperate with P9 absent strong evidence they are selfish; treat the reported defection as unverified. Use direct encounters to update beliefs, and favor cooperation when it supports good-player welfare.
Cooperate with likely-good players to support shared welfare; weigh reported actions as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with P7 given the credible report of mutual cooperation. Treat direct defections as strong evidence of selfishness, while accounting for reports that P6 cooperated against a defection.

Defect: it pays more than cooperation against either action. P2 and P8 cooperated against my D, strong evidence they are not selfish; D choices are suggestive but not conclusive, and the leader’s other claims are unverified.
Choose D to maximize my payoff in this simultaneous encounter. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions and the leader’s unverified claims.
Defect against P5: their defection against my cooperation is strong evidence of selfishness, and this is the final round. Cooperate with likely-good players to support their shared welfare.
Cooperate with P7, whose prior cooperation strongly indicates they are good; cooperation maximizes their and my combined good-player payoff.

Cooperate with P6 based on our mutual cooperation; prioritize shared welfare among good players. Defect against likely selfish players when it protects good-player welfare, while treating unverified claims cautiously.
Defect against P10 given their prior defection against my cooperation; observed cooperation is strong evidence of goodness, while defection raises but does not settle selfishness beliefs.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. Prioritize reliable encounter evidence: cooperation against my D rules out selfishness; defections and unverified claims leave uncertainty.
Cooperate with P3, whose prior cooperation is strong evidence they are good; mutual cooperation maximizes welfare when both are good.
Cooperate with P2, whose prior cooperation strongly suggests they are good. Treat defections and unverified reports as evidence, not proof, when estimating other roles.
Defect against P9 given repeated defections against cooperation; cooperate with likely-good players to preserve shared welfare. Treat ambiguous and indirect evidence cautiously.

Defect for the higher payoff against either action. P2, P6, and P8 are very likely good based on cooperation evidence; the six opponents who chose D remain uncertain, with beliefs reflecting the conditioned count prior.
Defect to maximize my payoff. Treat observed C against D as evidence the player is not selfish, since selfish players strictly prefer D; leave D-observing players uncertain.
Cooperated with likely-good players to support shared welfare, and used observed defections as evidence when deciding to defect. Treated mutual defections and unverified claims cautiously.

Cooperated with likely-good players to support shared welfare; used observed actions to update beliefs and defected when suspicion seemed high. Mutual cooperation was strong evidence of good intent, while defection was suggestive but not conclusive.

Cooperated with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare. Used direct encounter actions as strongest evidence, treated public claims cautiously, and defected when selfishness seemed likely.
Cooperated with likely-good players to support shared welfare and defected against likely-selfish opponents, updating from direct encounters and treating unverified claims cautiously.
Defected every round because defection strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
